title: Rectangular beam
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and a translation vector of zero, zero, and zero. For the first face, draw the first loop by starting at the origin and drawing a line to the point zero point one zero seven one, zero, then to zero point one zero seven one, zero point zero two one four, and back to the origin. Draw the second loop starting at the point zero point zero zero two one, zero point zero zero two one, and draw lines to zero point one zero five, zero point zero zero two one, then to zero point one zero five, zero point zero one nine three, and back to the starting point. Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point one zero seven one. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same vector. Extrude the sketch zero point seven five units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The resulting rectangular beam has a length of zero point one zero seven one four two eight five seven one four two eight five seven one five units, a width of zero point zero two one four two eight five seven one four two eight five seven one four three units, and a height of zero point seven five units, with slightly rounded edges.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the outer and inner loops of the sketch
outer_loop = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (0.1071, 0.0),
    (0.1071, 0.0214),
    (0.0, 0.0214),
    (0.0, 0.0)
]

inner_loop = [
    (0.0021, 0.0021),
    (0.105, 0.0021),
    (0.105, 0.0193),
    (0.0021, 0.0193),
    (0.0021, 0.0021)
]

# Create the sketch
r = r.polyline(outer_loop).close().polyline(inner_loop).close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) and translation vector (0, 0, 0) suggest
# a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis.
# However, since the translation vector is (0, 0, 0), we only need to consider the rotations.
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# Final model
r = r

# Display the model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1071, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1071, 0.0214) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0214) \
     .close() \
     .moveTo(0.0027, 0.0027) \
     .lineTo(0.1045, 0.0027) \
     .lineTo(0.1045, 0.0188) \
     .lineTo(0.0027, 0.0188) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

import cadquery as cq

# Part 1: Rectangular Object
part_1 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0.107142857).lineTo(0, 0.107142857).close().extrude(0.021428571)

# Part 2: Cylindrical Cutouts
part_2 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0.75, 0.053571429).circle(0.001785714).extrude(-0.010714286, combine=False)

# Combine part_1 and part_2
r = part_1.cut(part_2)
